headline: How will you pay for year one?
body: Three ways to get going. Each one costs you something: a slice of the company, or time.

options.label: Take money from Alder Lane Partners
options.detail: Marcus Delacroix and the people who follow him in. Cash in three weeks, opinions forever.
options.storyHeadline: Alder Lane Partners leads the seed round
options.mentorHint: The cash is real. The weekly calls that come with it are the problem.

options.label: Join Kestrel Group
options.detail: A smaller stake for a smaller check. Three months of Karim Okonjo telling you what's wrong, then a room full of investors.
options.mentorHint: Three months of being told what's wrong. Some of it will be.

options.label: Fund it yourself
options.detail: Do freelance work two days a week to pay for the other three. Slower, but nobody owns a piece of you.
options.mentorHint: You'll be fine. That's the catch — you'll be fine forever.

headline: Year one, take two
body: You already decided how much of your own money goes in. What's left is how fast you spend it.

options.label: Hire the team you need, now
options.detail: Spend fast and staff up immediately — the capital's already committed, so put it to work.
options.storyHeadline: Staffed up hard out of the gate
options.mentorHint: Move this fast and something breaks. It usually still works out.

options.label: Build the foundation first
options.detail: Get the basics right before you scale — slower out of the gate, steadier once it's moving.
options.storyHeadline: Took it slow and built the foundation
options.mentorHint: Nothing breaks. Also, nothing moves very fast.

options.label: Call in old favors
options.detail: The relationships from last time are still worth something — investors, customers, hires who'll answer the phone.
options.storyHeadline: Called in every favor from the last company
options.mentorHint: Everyone remembers you. Not everyone remembers fondly.
